In [[mathematics]], a '''quartan prime''' is a [[prime number]] of the form ''x''<sup>4</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;''y''<sup>4</sup> where ''x'' and ''y'' are positive [[integer]]s. [[parity (mathematics)|Odd]] quartan primes are of the form&nbsp;16''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1.

For example, 17 is the smallest odd quartan prime: 1<sup>4</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;2<sup>4</sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;1&nbsp;+&nbsp;16&nbsp;=&nbsp;17.

With the exception of 2 (''x'' = ''y'' = 1), one of ''x'' and ''y'' will be odd, and the other [[parity (mathematics)|even]]. If both are odd or both are even, the result will be even, and 2 is the only even prime. 

The first few quartan primes are:
:[[2 (number)|2]], [[17 (number)|17]], [[97 (number)|97]], [[257 (number)|257]], [[337 (number)|337]], [[641 (number)|641]], [[881 (number)|881]], … {{OEIS|id=A002645}}.
